summary: OBJECT at 2 SHOULD-FIX. The measurement layer of this draft is sound: every one of the ten digest citations reproduces from disk, the subject is unmoved at 0444, HEAD is unmoved, the Stage A pair is genuinely dual ACCEPT 0/0 at mode 0444, and every live-state assertion (required-now 28 of 28, owners 32 of 32, last gate row DR-G32, DR-G31 lead token OPEN, DR-104 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, file 08 carries G31, condition 2 at 4 of 32, condition 4 MET, condition 5 last) reproduces at file 08. Every prohibition in the dispatch and the prompt is honoured in the draft text, the D-167-through-D-207 non-unwrite span is complete at 41 entries with D-168 present and no gap, and the draft does not claim that D-056 gates 2 and 3 fail. I ran all fourteen named attacks and refuted all fourteen. The two findings are in the disclosure layer, not the measurement layer. First, clause 4 records a single Stage A advisory as travelling as honesty work when the Stage A pair carried four; the three Claude advisories are dropped and the singular framing misstates the Stage A outcome, breaking the convention D-207 and thirteen earlier entries observed. Second, the measured-inputs table pins two of the three frozen predecessors whose standing the draft asserts, dropping v3 while the prose treats v3 and v4 as one pair and the table labels v4 by exactly the category v3 shares. Both are cheap to repair and neither falsifies a pinned measurement, so neither is a MUST-FIX.

shouldFix.text: Advisory CODEX-G31-V5-ADV-1 travels as honesty work.
shouldFix.finding: The Stage A pair carried four advisories, not one. Codex returned CODEX-G31-V5-ADV-1; Claude 2 returned CLAUDE-G31-V5-ADV-1 (.findingDisposition does not disposition the advisory whose repair v5 actually performed), CLAUDE-G31-V5-ADV-2 (.purpose miscategorises predecessorV1.role's carried 'This v2' label as a v3 self-reference, and does not disclose the namingV1.role edit), and CLAUDE-G31-V5-ADV-3 (.registerRowNote names the earliest frozen predecessor where every parallel field names the current one or is exhaustive). The draft names one of the four and drops three. The singular framing compounds it: 'Advisory CODEX-G31-V5-ADV-1 travels as honesty work' reads to a later reader as the complete Stage A advisory set, so the entry does not merely omit three items, it misstates the Stage A outcome as carrying a single advisory.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The honesty-work clause is the mechanism by which a Stage A advisory survives adoption into the permanent record; an advisory that is not named in it does not travel. Three genuine observations about the artifact this entry freezes would be lost at adoption.
shouldFix.conventionEvidence: This breaks the settled practice of the corpus. I measured every entry from D-120 to D-207 whose subject carried Stage A advisories: sixteen entries. Fourteen name every advisory both reviewers raised, including all five cross-reviewer cases — D-124 names CLAUDE-V16-A1/A2 and MCICV16-A1; D-126 names all three CLAUDE-HEA25 and all three HAE25-ADV; D-137 names both CLAUDE-PPBS-V5 advisories and PPBSV4-ADV-1; D-138 names CLAUDE-PAC-V2-ADV-1 and DR131V1-ADV-1; D-146 names CLAUDE-PONAL-V1-ADV1 and PAL-V1-A1. The two exceptions, D-122 and D-145, are old. D-207, the immediately preceding entry and the nearest precedent in both form and date, names both of its Stage A advisories and additionally carries a standing advisory forward.
shouldFix.graded: SHOULD-FIX, not MUST-FIX. It falsifies no pinned measurement, misdirects no act, and violates no dispatch prohibition. It is a disclosure defect in the entry's own account of its Stage A evidence.

advisories.detail: 'After D-167, G31 is live and required-now is 28.' Both conjuncts are true of the present, and the sentence does not literally say D-167 set required-now to 28, so this is not a false statement. But the sentence places both facts under one 'After D-167' and a reader may take the cardinality as D-167's effect. It was not: D-167 recorded cardinality 27, and D-169 took it to 28 by adding G32 — a distinction file 08 line 417 preserves by listing D-167 and D-169 as separate naming decisions, and one the Stage A Claude verdict tested explicitly against the subject artifact and found correctly handled there. Held at advisory rather than SHOULD-FIX for three reasons. It sits in the narrative section, not in a pinned measurement or a decision clause. The draft's operative statement of the number, at line 70, is a live remeasurement carrying no attribution at all and is exactly right. And the entry directs no act on the strength of the attribution. Repair if convenient: 'After D-167, G31 is live; after D-169, required-now is 28.'
